headline_en: ArchSpace, Agent Memory, and Diffusion Verifiers Lead Today's AI Research
lede_en: Today's research agenda centers on making model development more transparent, evaluable, and agentic. ArchSpace offers a public platform for recording and scaling architecture experiments, while new work on diffusion regeneration and cost-aware memory pushes autonomous systems toward better reasoning and efficiency. Meanwhile, coding assistant vendors shipped incremental reliability and usability fixes rather than new capabilities.

sections_en.title: Architecture & Evaluation Infrastructure
sections_en.body: ArchSpace tackles the opacity of LLM architecture research by providing a public record where proposals can be reviewed and evaluated with scaling-law predictions, lowering the cost of identifying ideas that truly scale. In a complementary move, DiVR addresses decoding-time uncertainty in diffusion language models by training a verifier to predict when a partial sequence will succeed, lifting LLaDA-8B-Base accuracy from 35.3% to 43.4% on reasoning benchmarks without retraining the generator. Together these projects signal a maturing evaluation culture: cheaper, more systematic testing of both architectural and decoding hypotheses.

sections_en.title: Agent Engineering
sections_en.body: AgentSSL recasts semi-supervised learning as a program search problem for MLE agents, showing agents can combine established techniques to beat human baselines but exposing a 47% performance drop when selection relies on noisy agent feedback. CoReMem gives coding agents a cost-aware memory that estimates the value of stored segments against future tasks, improving long-horizon repository work without ignoring read/write overhead. Internalizing investment mandates extends this agent autonomy to finance by embedding regulatory constraints into continuous-action RL through reparameterized sampling. The common thread is agents that learn their own constraints—data, memory, or compliance—rather than relying on post-hoc fixes.

sections_en.title: Model Releases & Developer Tooling
sections_en.body: Today's release notes from DeepSeek, Qwen, and Moonshot emphasize workflow continuity and reliability. DeepSeek Harness v0.2.2-rc.3 adds an experimental plugin to import past conversations and fixes a Windows auto-reopen bug; qwen-code improves visibility of background tasks and hardens CI, enrollment, and channel handling across desktop and SDK; kimi-code speeds session restoration and improves terminal transcript grouping. These are incremental patches, but they reflect how much of the current coding-agent race is being fought on usability and robustness.
